newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian security arrest three rights activists.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian security arrest three rights activists.

text.p: Nigeria's security officials have arrested three members of the human rights organisation Amnesty International, their colleague said on Friday.
"The three officers were arrested this morning and taken to the Ojuelegba police station," Michael Onyeka, Campaign and Outreach Coordinator of the Lagos chapter, told Reuters.

He said Patrice Vahard, development officer west and central Africa, Lagos executive secretary Eke Ubije and group development officer David Omonzuafo were arrested in Lagos on their way to address diplomats on the human rights situation in Nigeria and Africa.

"They smuggled a note out of the police cell to inform us of their arrest. But the police at the station said our members had been transferred elsewhere and (they) do not know of their whereabouts," he said.
There has been no official confirmation of the arrests.
Nigeria has been under fire for alleged rights abuses and lack of democracy.
Amnesty International's General Secretary Pierre Sane on Friday in Johannesburg criticised developed nations for their approach to the human rights situation in Africa.
Onyeka said Vahard was to read the diplomats the speech Sane delivered in Johannesburg.
Amnesty on Wednesday launched a campaign against Nigeria's military government for alleged rights violations. It released a report accusing the military of being openly contemptuous of human rights.
